 Judgment

The appeal is filed under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 by the appellant - KSRTC,
challenging the judgment and award dated 20th November 2015 passed in MVC No.612/2014 on the file of XXIII Additional Small Causes Judge and XXI A.C.M.M. & Member, MACT, Court of Small Causes, Bengaluru (hereinafter referred to as 'the Tribunal' for brevity), questioning the quantum of compensation.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. Heard the arguments of learned counsel for the appellant - KSRTC and learned counsel for the respondent and perused the material placed before the Court.
3.
The fatal accident, death and coverage of insurance are not in dispute.

4. The Tribunal has awarded compensation under various heads as follows:
NC: 2024:KHC:21381 i) Loss of dependency : Rs.6,72,000-00 ii) Loss of love and affection : Rs.1,00,000-00 iii) Loss of future prospects : Rs.3,36,000-00 iv) Funeral expenses : Rs. 25,000-00 v) Loss of estate : Rs. 33,600-00 vi) Transportation of dead body : Rs. 10,000-00 ............................
Karnataka State Road Transport ... vs Vasantha on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/186959266/
2

The Tribunal considered the income of the deceased at Rs.7,000/- per month and deducted 50% towards personal expenses and adopted the appropriate multiplier according to the age of the deceased and awarded compensation of Rs.11,76,600/-
alongwith interest at 9% per annum.

5. Considering the year of accident as 2013, the notional income ought to have been taken at Rs.8,000/- per month as per the notional income chart as recognized by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, but the Tribunal has taken income at Rs.7,000/- per month and awarded compensation of Rs.6,72,000/- towards 'loss of dependency'.
Though on other heads, amount of compensation awarded is little bit higher, NC: 2024:KHC:21381 that is taken care of by the income taken by the Tribunal on the lesser side.
Therefore, the total compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper and the same does not call for interference.
6. The Tribunal has granted interest at 9% per annum.

The same is liable to be scaled down to 6%
per annum.
Only to this extent, appeal filed by the KSRTC is liable to be allowed in part.

7. In the result, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i) The appeal is allowed in part.
ii) The impugned judgment and award dated 20th November 2015 passed in MVC No.612/2014 on the file of the on the file of XXIII Additional Small Causes Judge and XXI A.C.M.M. & Member, MACT, Court of Small Causes, Bengaluru, is modified only in respect of interest awarded by the Tribunal.

The interest is scaled down from 9%
per annum to 6% per NC: 2024:KHC:21381 annum.
The total compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper and the same is kept intact.
iii) The amount in deposit, if any before this Court shall be transferred to the Tribunal forthwith.
iv) Draw the award accordingly.
v) Registry is directed to return the Trial Court Records to the Tribunal, along with certified copy of the judgment passed by this Court forthwith.

Sd/-
